story_clusters.headline: 10 Bills passed in Karnataka Legislature without debate amid BJP protest on last day of session
story_clusters.summary: The Karnataka Legislature passed 10 Bills without debate on the final day of the session amid protests by the BJP. Separately, the Karnataka Assembly approved a Bill allowing the government to use portions of parks for infrastructure, with the BJP alleging collusion between Chief Minister Shivakumar and Adani. Meanwhile, in Telangana, 20 Congress MLAs demanded the sacking of Minister Konda Surekha over a remark made by her daughter, while a police official was suspended in a case involving her former OSD.

articles.title: SC Sets Aside HC Interference in Arbitration, Directs Tribunal to Decide Non-Signatory Status
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India set aside orders passed by the Gauhati High Court under Article 227, stating that jurisdictional objections under Section 16 of the Arbitration Act should typically await a remedy under Section 34. The Court directed the arbitration tribunal to independently determine whether a non-signatory party can be bound by the arbitration agreement. The ruling clarifies the interplay between judicial interference and tribunal autonomy in arbitration cases.
articles.raw_summary: Supreme Court sets aside Gauhati HC orders under Article 227, holding that Section 16 jurisdictional objections ordinarily await Section 34 remedy and directing the Tribunal to decide non-signatory status independently. The post SC Sets Aside HC Interference in Arbitration, Directs Tribunal to Decide Non-Signatory Status appeared first on TaxGuru .

articles.title: Section 16 Arbitration Order Cannot Be Re-examined in Writ Jurisdiction: SC Dismisses Appeal
articles.summary: The Supreme Court ruled that a Section 16 arbitration order on contract stamping cannot be re-examined under writ jurisdiction. The court dismissed an appeal, leaving the stamping issue open for potential challenge under Section 34 of the Arbitration Act. This decision clarifies the limits of judicial review in arbitration disputes.
articles.raw_summary: Supreme Court holds that writ jurisdiction cannot be used to re-examine a Section 16 arbitration order on contract stamping and leaves the stamping issue open for Section 34. The post Section 16 Arbitration Order Cannot Be Re-examined in Writ Jurisdiction: SC Dismisses Appeal appeared first on TaxGuru .

articles.title: Karnataka HC Upholds Quashing of Assessment Ignoring DRP Directions
articles.summary: The Karnataka High Court upheld a decision by the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) to quash a tax assessment against Flextronics for failing to follow binding directions issued by the Dispute Resolution Panel (DRP) under Section 144C of the Income-tax Act. The ruling reinforces the legal obligation of tax authorities to adhere to DRP directives, setting a precedent for future tax assessments in India. The case highlights the importance of procedural compliance in tax administration.

Additionally, remittances for the upkeep of close relatives accounted for $287 million, while investments in equity and debt attracted $456 million from Indian residents.

articles.title: Hydel project shutdown triggers power crisis in J&K
articles.summary: The shutdown of the Baglihar hydel project in Jammu & Kashmir has led to a severe power shortage, with the region facing a deficit of nearly 900MW. The Baglihar units, critical power sources on the Chenab river, have been largely unavailable, exacerbating the summer peak demand of 2,500MW and winter demand of 3,000MW. The prolonged outage has widened the power deficit, raising concerns about the region's energy security.
articles.raw_summary: The prolonged shutdown has widened the region’s power deficit. Jammu Kashmir’s peak electricity demand stands at about 2,500MW in summer and 3,000MW in winter. With both Baglihar units largely unavailable for most of the past week, Jammu Kashmir faced a shortfall of nearly 900MW. Built on the Chenab river, Baglihar stages I and II are among Jammu Kashmir’s key power sources.

articles.title: Wars are now hitting more than 43% of the world’s oil supply

This has increased reliance on U.S. oil, depleted global reserves after emergency releases, and contributed to rising fuel prices driving global inflation. The situation highlights vulnerabilities in energy supply chains that could impact India's policy decisions on fuel imports, reserves, and inflation control.
articles.raw_summary: Currently, more than 40% of the world's oil supply is derived from conflict-ridden regions. Ongoing tensions in the Gulf and Ukraine have reduced refining abilities by 10%. As a result, reliance on U.S. oil has surged, leading to a depletion of global reserves after emergency releases have concluded. This situation has made rising fuel prices a significant contributor to inflation across the globe.
